title: Veterans’ Affairs Legislation Amendment (Enhanced Family Support) Bill 2022
short_title: Veterans’ Affairs Legislation Amendment (Enhanced Family Support) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would widen access to the veterans' Family Support Package and expand the assistance available to eligible veterans and families facing difficult life circumstances.
It would extend support across three veterans' compensation laws and allow instruments to set additional eligibility rules, overall funding caps and periods of assistance.
The substantive changes would start on 1 July 2022, with access no longer dependent on warlike service or participation in a rehabilitation program.
changes: Available assistance would expand to include household services, skills development and academic or extracurricular support for children.
Separate financial limits for service categories would give way to overall caps set through legislative instruments.
Family support payments would be exempt from income tax and excluded from income assessments under social security law.
summary.affected: Eligible veterans, family members, bereaved partners and the commissions administering veterans' benefits would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Kenneth Neumann
speeches.brief: The Labor Party supports the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Enhanced Family Support) Bill 2022, which expands eligibility for family support packages, harmonises the MRCA, DRCA and VA Acts, and implements recommendations from a veteran suicide inquiry and the Productivity Commission, effective 1 July; the speaker criticised the government for delaying the bill until just before an election.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Gee
speeches.brief: The Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Enhanced Family Support) Bill 2022 expands eligibility and increases financial assistance for veteran families, providing up to $12,500 over two years for at-risk families, additional payments per child, and up to $27,835 per year for widowed partners, in response to the 2017 Senate inquiry into veteran suicide and the 2019 Productivity Commission report.
